Every page below shows live previews with ready-to-copy code. Accordion Build collapsible content sections with accordion classes and modifiers. Alert Show alert messages that inform users about success, info, warning, or danger states, with icons, links, and dismissible options. Avatar Display user avatars with images, initials, or icons. Change sizes, shapes, and colors, or group them into stacked avatar lists. Badge Add badges to show counts, labels, or statuses. Use colors, outline and pill styles, links, and notification dots to add context. Breadcrumb A breadcrumb trail for the current page location, with separators, icons and a muted style. ` -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Docs callouts | Tabler UI Documentation (https://docs.tabler.io/ui/getting-started/callouts) 【turn9search5】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last week; # Docs callouts Callouts pull one sentence out of the page flow, such as a prerequisite or a warning. The docs ship five of them for any MDX page. ## Overview A callout is a short aside inside a docs page. It carries something a reader must not miss while scanning: a step to do first, a mistake that costs an hour, a limit of the library. Callouts belong to the documentation, not to the Tabler UI package. For an alert inside a product interface, use the alert component instead. ## Variants Five variants cover what a docs page needs. The icon and the border carry the state color; the text stays body color, so a callout never depends on color alone. ### Info Use it for context and prerequisites - something to know or to do before the rest of the page makes sense. Read the installation guide first The examples on this page assume Tabler is already installed and the stylesheet is on the page. ` The examples on this page assume Tabler is already installed. ` ### Tip Use it for advice that makes the task easier, but is not required to finish it. Set the theme before init Some plugins keep the skin they were created with, so switching the theme afterwards has no effect. ### Warning Use it when missing the information breaks something later - a deprecation, a load order, a license limit. `@import` is on its way out It still compiles, but Dart Sass marks it as deprecated and will remove it in Sass 3.0. ### Danger Use it for what cannot be undone or what is unsafe - lost data, leaked credentials. Use a public token only A secret token must never be sent to the browser. Limit the token to your own domains. ### Note A callout with no title is body text only. Use it for a short aside that needs no heading. Tabler ships the compiled CSS in `dist/css`, so a project without a Sass pipeline can still use it.
